When your application uses Tailwind CSS, you can use the same Tailwind CSS classes in an advanced theme. The Tailwind CSS build scans the theme templates for class names and writes the stylesheet that the [[hosted login pages]] use. The FusionAuth CLI uploads the templates and the stylesheet to FusionAuth.

This guide covers Tailwind CSS 4 and Tailwind CSS 3. Tailwind CSS 4 supports Safari 16.4 and later, Chrome 111 and later, and Firefox 128 and later. When the users of your login pages need older browsers, use Tailwind CSS 3.

## Prerequisites

* Node.js 20 or later

## Set Up FusionAuth

<Steps>

1. Navigate to <Breadcrumb>Customization -> Themes</Breadcrumb> and click <Breadcrumb>Add</Breadcrumb>. Enter a **Name** for the theme and click <Breadcrumb>Save</Breadcrumb>.

   <Screenshot id="theme-add-advanced" url="/admin/theme/add" alt="The form to create a theme in the Admin UI." />

1. Navigate to <Breadcrumb>Settings -> API Keys</Breadcrumb> and click <Breadcrumb>Add</Breadcrumb>. Select the `GET` and `PATCH` permissions for `/api/theme/`, and click <Breadcrumb>Save</Breadcrumb>.

   <Screenshot id="theme-create-api-key" url="/admin/api-key/add" alt="The form to create an API key, with the theme permissions highlighted.">
     <Highlight selector="[data-hl='api-theme-row']" />
   </Screenshot>

</Steps>

## Create the Project

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Tailwind CSS 4">

<Steps>

1. Create a Node.js project, and install the FusionAuth CLI and Tailwind CSS:

   ```shell-session
   mkdir fusionauth-tailwind
   cd fusionauth-tailwind
   npm init -y
   npm install @fusionauth/cli tailwindcss @tailwindcss/cli
   ```

1. Create `input.css` in the project root. The file imports Tailwind CSS, and **`@source`** adds the FreeMarker templates in the `tpl` directory to the build. Add your own classes to this file:

   ```css
   @import "tailwindcss";
   @source "./tpl";
   ```

1. Add the following scripts to `package.json`. Replace `<themeId>` and `<apiKey>` with the Id of the theme and the API key:

   ```json
   "scripts": {
     "watch:tailwind": "tailwindcss -i ./input.css -o ./tpl/stylesheet.css --watch",
     "watch:theme": "fusionauth theme:watch <themeId> -k <apiKey> -h http://localhost:9011"
   },
   ```

</Steps>

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Tailwind CSS 3">

<Steps>

1. Create a Node.js project, install the FusionAuth CLI and Tailwind CSS, and create a Tailwind CSS configuration file:

   ```shell-session
   mkdir fusionauth-tailwind
   cd fusionauth-tailwind
   npm init -y
   npm install @fusionauth/cli tailwindcss@3
   npx tailwindcss init
   ```

1. Set **`content`** in `tailwind.config.js` to the FreeMarker templates in the `tpl` directory:

   ```js
   /** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
   module.exports = {
     content: ['./tpl/*.ftl'],
     theme: {
       extend: {}
     },
     plugins: []
   }
   ```

1. Create `input.css` in the project root. The file imports the Tailwind CSS base styles, components, and utilities. Add your own classes to this file:

   ```css
   @tailwind base;
   @tailwind components;
   @tailwind utilities;
   ```

1. Add the following scripts to `package.json`. Replace `<themeId>` and `<apiKey>` with the Id of the theme and the API key:

   ```json
   "scripts": {
     "watch:tailwind": "tailwindcss -i ./input.css -o ./tpl/stylesheet.css --watch",
     "watch:theme": "fusionauth theme:watch <themeId> -k <apiKey> -h http://localhost:9011"
   },
   ```

</Steps>

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Prepare the Theme

<Steps>

1. Download the theme. Replace `<themeId>` and `<apiKey>` again:

   ```shell-session
   npx fusionauth theme:download <themeId> -k <apiKey> -h http://localhost:9011
   ```

   The CLI writes the templates to `.ftl` files in the `tpl` directory, and the stylesheet to `tpl/stylesheet.css`.

1. Remove the `link` tag for the default FusionAuth stylesheet from the `head` macro in `tpl/helpers.ftl`. The default styles conflict with Tailwind CSS. Recent themes link `fusionauth-hosted.css`:

   ```ftl
   <link rel="stylesheet" href="${request.contextPath}/css/entrypoints/fusionauth-hosted.css?version=${version}"/>
   ```

   Older themes link `fusionauth-style.css` instead.

1. Upload the theme to apply the change to `tpl/helpers.ftl`:

   ```shell-session
   npx fusionauth theme:upload <themeId> -k <apiKey> -h http://localhost:9011
   ```

</Steps>

## Edit the Theme

Run each of the following scripts in a separate terminal:

* `npm run watch:tailwind` rebuilds `tpl/stylesheet.css` when a template changes.
* `npm run watch:theme` uploads the templates and the stylesheet to FusionAuth when a file in the `tpl` directory changes.

When a template uses a Tailwind CSS class, the build adds the class to the stylesheet:

```html
<div class="bg-gray-200">
  <h1 class="text-2xl">Hello World</h1>
</div>
```

To preview the theme, navigate to <Breadcrumb>Customization -> Themes</Breadcrumb>, choose the theme, and click <IconButton icon="view" />.

<Screenshot id="theme-preview-menu" url="/admin/theme/" alt="The themes list, with the preview button highlighted.">
  <Highlight selector="[data-hl='theme-preview']" />
</Screenshot>

<Screenshot id="theme-preview-oauth-authorize" url="/admin/theme/view/75a068fd-e94b-451a-9aeb-3ddb9a3b5987#oauth2Authorize" height={1100} alt="The preview of the themed login page." />

When the application also uses React, you can copy the markup of the application's components into the templates. For more information, see [Match FusionAuth Themes to a React Application](/docs/theme/advanced-themes/react).

## Add DaisyUI

DaisyUI is a Tailwind CSS plugin with prebuilt components, color themes, light and dark modes, and right-to-left support. DaisyUI 5 requires Tailwind CSS 4. With Tailwind CSS 3, use DaisyUI 2, which the [FusionAuth example DaisyUI theme](https://github.com/FusionAuth/fusionauth-example-theme-tailwind-daisyui/) uses.

The example theme sets up light and dark modes, and includes templates for the following pages:

* Log in
* Log out
* Registration
* Forgot password

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="DaisyUI 5">

<Steps>

1. Install the plugin:

   ```shell-session
   npm install daisyui
   ```

1. Add the plugin to `input.css`:

   ```css
   @import "tailwindcss";
   @source "./tpl";
   @plugin "daisyui";
   ```

</Steps>

To use the color scheme of the example theme, set the themes in `input.css`. **`--default`** sets the light theme, and **`--prefersdark`** sets the theme for browsers in dark mode. The `daisyui/theme` block changes the primary color of the `business` theme, and the `@theme` block adds the progress bar animation that the example templates use:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@source "./tpl";

@plugin "daisyui" {
  themes: corporate --default, business --prefersdark;
}

@plugin "daisyui/theme" {
  name: "business";
  prefersdark: true;
  --color-primary: #c891f2;
}

@theme {
  --animate-progressBar: progressBar 10s ease-in 1;
  @keyframes progressBar {
    0% { width: 0%; }
    100% { width: 100%; }
  }
}
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="DaisyUI 2">

<Steps>

1. Install the plugin:

   ```shell-session
   npm install daisyui@2
   ```

1. Add the plugin to `tailwind.config.js`:

   ```js
   module.exports = {
     content: ['./tpl/*.ftl'],
     theme: {
       extend: {}
     },
     plugins: [
       require('daisyui')
     ]
   }
   ```

</Steps>

To change the color scheme of the example theme, edit **`daisyui.themes`** and **`daisyui.darkTheme`** in `tailwind.config.js`:

```js {29} [1-21]
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: ['./tpl/*.ftl'],
  theme: {
    extend: {
        keyframes: {
            progressBar: {
                "0%": {
                    width: "0%"
                },
                "100%": {
                    width: "100%"
                }
            }
        },
        animation: {
            progressBar: "progressBar 10s ease-in 1"
        }
    }
  },
  plugins: [require("daisyui")],

  daisyui: {
      themes: [
          'corporate',
          {
            business: {
                ...require("daisyui/src/colors/themes")["[data-theme=business]"],
                'primary': '#c891f2'
            }
          }
      ],
      darkTheme: 'business'
  }
}
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

Use DaisyUI components in the templates:

```html
<div class="bg-gray-200">
  <h1 class="text-2xl">Hello World</h1>
  <div class="p-4">
    <button class="btn btn-primary">Primary</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

To create a color theme, use the [DaisyUI Theme Generator](https://daisyui.com/theme-generator/).
